newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo govt says to exclude DKB from bond syndicate.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo govt says to exclude DKB from bond syndicate.

text.p: The Tokyo metropolitan government has decided to exclude scandal-hit Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd from its bond underwriting syndicate starting from the July issue, a metropolitan government official said on Thursday.
"We have decided to exclude DKB from our bond underwriting syndicate for the time being," the official said.

The decision followed a Ministry of Finance (MOF) announcement on Wednesday that that it was suspending DKB from Japanese government bond (JGB) auctions and JGB underwriting "for the time being", beginning with the next 10-year JGB auction due later this month.
"Certainly we used the MOF decision as a reference, but it was our independent decision," the official said.
He added that the Tokyo government's July bond issue would be around 50 billion yen, and that DKB's share of the underwriting syndicate is 7.2 percent.

The official said the metropolitan government's decision about when to re-instate DKB would depend on what further moves MOF may take against the bank, as well as developments in the ongoing investigation against it.

MOF said in a statement on Wednesday that, if a legal complaint is filed with prosecutors against DKB, the suspension would remain in effect until the ministry implements subsequent administrative penalties against DKB.

In May, MOF suspended Nomura Securities Co Ltd from JGB auctions and underwriting until the implementation of administrative penalties which may be proposed by the Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission (SESC).
DKB and Nomura have both been implicated in a scandal involving suspected illegal payoffs to racketeers.

Officials with the city governments of Yokohama and Osaka said early on Thursday that they are considering whether to exclude DKB from underwriting syndicates for their municipal bonds, but that a decision had yet to be reached.

The largest amount of outstanding municipal bonds as of the end of March this year were those issued by the Tokyo metropolitan government, a total of 3.5662 trillion yen, followed by Osaka and Yokohama.

The Home Affairs Ministry issued an advisory on Wednesday that prefectural governments and designated cities should take "appropriate measures" in regard to DKB and their underwriting syndicates in light of the bank's suspension from JGB auctions and underwriting.
